thread:
nisha: hey team — spotted a puzzling HF->Redwood chat_template conversion that trims metadata and causes weird tokenization; repro below

kevin: hit me with the minimal repro pls

nisha: here's the Jinja chat_template that some model bundles publish:```
{"format": "chat", "template": "{% raw %}{% if system %}{{ system }}\n\n---\n{% endif %}{% for m in messages %}- {{ m.role }}: {{ m.content }}\n{% endfor %}{% endraw %}"}```

nisha: when system is an empty string the converter produces no system role at all (expected maybe an empty system token or explicit sentinel). downstream Redwood prompt builder then treats the first user message as if it were system-prefixed in some model tokenizers which add special BOS/role tokens. result: role bleed and a ~2-4 token shift in context, sometimes changing decoding in quantized runs.

olivia: interesting — do we have a failing eval or is this from manual inspection?

nisha: both. small eval suite (sanity/formatting) shows a 3% regression on instruction-following benchmarks for one LLM after conversion. manual diff of tokenized sequences shows extra special tokens on HF side vs our converted prompt. e.g. run:```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('some-hf-llm')
print(tok.encode('<s>System:</s>'))
```
we see model-specific sentinels that our converter doesn't inject.

marco: could this be a tokenizer/config.json mismatch? HF bundles sometimes set "add_bos_token": true or special_tokens_map in config.json. we may be ignoring that when rendering chat_template -> single prompt string.

nisha: exactly. config.json often has ``"bos_token":"<s>", "eos_token":"</s>", "additional_special_tokens": ["<|system|>"]`` and the template expects those tokens to be present. but the Jinja template uses a conditional system block rather than an explicit token sentinel; when empty, the template drops the text and there's no placeholder for the special token. converter should synthesize the correct sentinel or preserve an explicit empty-block marker.

jen: is this only about empty system? what about role-order differences (assistant vs assistant_reply)?

nisha: role-name mapping is another axis. HF chat_templates sometimes call roles "assistant", "user", "system"; some models expect token-level markers like `<|assistant|>` vs `<|endofassistant|>`. Our current mapper only normalizes role names but doesn't insert model-specific special tokens.

kevin: short term: can we change the converter to emit a visible sentinel when system evaluates to empty string, like `<<SYSTEM>>` then replace `<<SYSTEM>>` with the model's configured special token from config.json if present? avoids silent deletion.

olivia: doable. patch plan: 1) detect conditional-empty blocks in Jinja AST at conversion time; 2) emit a fixed placeholder `__RW_EMPTY_SYSTEM__`; 3) during tokenization/render step consult config.json / tokenizer.special_tokens_map to replace placeholder with actual token(s).

marco: also care about quantized runs: q4_xx models sometimes have tokenizer peculiarities; we should run the tokenizer before and after quantization to confirm no token-id remapping. failing case showed different token ids for same str when using fused tokenizer wrappers in our runtime.

nisha: noted. repro steps I ran: 1) use original HF chat_template + messages payload (system = "") 2) convert via our jinja->rw converter 3) call tokenizer.encode on both original expected prompt (with synthetic sentinel) and converted prompt 4) compare token ids and decoded text. I can paste a sample diff if helpful.

kevin: please paste the diff here (short) and add to the model-onboarding test harness as a unit test. we need this guarded.

nisha: diff snippet:```
# expected (with sentinel injected) tokens: [1, 234, 98, ...] # includes <|system|> id 42
# converted (no sentinel): [1, 234, 99, ...] # shifted because tokenizer combined newline+role into different token
```

olivia: also let's ensure the converter respects `special_tokens_map` and `tokenizer_class` entries in config.json. some HF packs set `tokenizer_class: 'LlamaTokenizer'` but also add `pad_token` mapping that matters for batching.

marco: for rollout: add a small e2e check in onboarding pipeline: for every chat_template-based conversion, render two prompt variants (with and without explicit synthetic sentinel) and assert token sequences map to same logical role boundaries. fail onboarding if mismatch.

jen: could we just prefer to keep the original HF chat_template as an intermediate artifact and only render at runtime with the model tokenizer? pros/cons: keeps fidelity but moves complexity to runtime.

kevin: runtime cost matters — we prefer converter-level fixes so hosted endpoints get consistent prompt shapes. but for private deployments we may provide an option to keep original template. add flag `preserve_hf_template: bool` in onboarding manifest.

nisha: filed a small ticket RW-ML-823 with repro, attached sample model bundle, tokenizer logs, and quantized vs float token id diffs. I'll add the unit test and a suggested converter patch.

render-bot: deploy check: converter unit tests + onboarding integration — pipeline run queued (job id: ci-64231).

kevin: thanks. action items: nisha to open PR with placeholder injection + config.json lookup; marco to add tokenizer-id parity test for q4_* quantized variants; olivia to update onboarding docs to mention `preserve_hf_template`. we'll triage priority P2 for this week.

olivia: acked.

marco: if anyone hits other oddities with special tokens in model bundles ping me, I suspect multiple bundles silently rely on token-order hacks.

jen: thanks — good catch.
